pr_title: fix: fix nullable filter mask in group_by

issue_context.title: An error occurs when using filter in groupby.agg
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
pl.DataFrame({
    'name':['a'] * 3,
    'type':[None] * 3,
    'order':[1,2,3]
}).with_columns([
    pl.col('type').cast(pl.Int32)
]).group_by('name').agg([
    pl.col('order').n_unique().alias('n1'),
    pl.col('order').filter(pl.col('type') == 1).n_unique().alias('n2'),
    pl.col('order').filter(pl.col('type').is_null()).n_unique().alias('n3'),
    pl.col('order').filter(pl.col('type').is_not_null()).n_unique().alias('n4'),
])
```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

filter does not work

### Expected behavior

name	n1	n2	n3	n4
str	u32	u32	u32	u32
"a"	3	null	3	null


### Installed versions


comments:
It seems that by "error" you mean the `n2` column returns `3` instead of `null`?

It may be similar to #10204 (which references #9329 for a longer explanation) and you're looking for [`.eq_missing`](https://pola-rs.github.io/polars/py-polars/html/reference/expressions/api/polars.Expr.eq_missing.html#polars.Expr.eq_missing)?

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({
    'name':['a'] * 3,
    'type':[None] * 3,
    'order':[1, 2, 3]
}).with_columns(
    pl.col('type').cast(pl.Int32)
)

df.group_by('name').agg(
    pl.col('order').n_unique().alias('n1'),
    pl.col('order').filter(pl.col('type').eq_missing(1)).n_unique().alias('n2'),
    pl.col('order').filter(pl.col('type').is_null()).n_unique().alias('n3'),
    pl.col('order').filter(pl.col('type').is_not_null()).n_unique().alias('n4'),
)
```
```
shape: (1, 5)
┌──────┬─────┬──────┬─────┬──────┐
│ name ┆ n1  ┆ n2   ┆ n3  ┆ n4   │
│ ---  ┆ --- ┆ ---  ┆ --- ┆ ---  │
│ str  ┆ u32 ┆ u32  ┆ u32 ┆ u32  │
╞══════╪═════╪══════╪═════╪══════╡
│ a    ┆ 3   ┆ null ┆ 3   ┆ null │
└──────┴─────┴──────┴─────┴──────┘
```

@cmdlineluser But one could argue that:

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "name": ["a", "a", "a", "a"],
            "type": [None, None, None, None],
            "order": [1, 2, 3, 4],
        }
    )
assert df.select(pl.col("order").filter(pl.col("type").eq(1))).is_empty()
assert df.select(pl.col("order").filter(pl.col("type").eq_missing(1))).is_empty()
```
`eq & eq_missing` both given us an empty df.

While in agg context:
```python
out = (
        df.group_by("name", maintain_order=True)
        .agg([pl.col("order").filter(pl.col("type").eq(1)).alias("eq")])
        .select("eq")
    )
assert out.to_dict(False) == {"eq": [[1, 2, 3, 4]]}
```

IMO, the only difference between `eq` and `eq_missing` is that the latter propagates `null` value. That's to say, `None eq 1 is None` but `None eq_missing 1 is false`. But whether it is `None` or `false`, it should be filtered out.
BTW, `None eq None` should be `None`, but `None eq_missing None` should be `true`.
@ztsweet I think this is raised by design, see https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/11395.

review_comments: If `predicate` only has `null` and `true`, `all` will return `true` and return the non-filtered series directly, this looks a bit strange.  IIUC, value masked by `None` should also be filtered out. WDYT?
We should do the same as in the `select` context. I see that we only return the true values there. So yes this seems correct.
